title: Replicated Trials and Environmental Noise
objective: Separate genetic signal from position, room, season, management, and measurement effects using replication, randomization, blocking, and checks.
coreScience: A single plant in a single location cannot separate genotype from environment. Replication means independent experimental units receiving the same genotype or family. Repeated measurements on one plant improve temporal detail but are not biological replicates. Clones can provide genetically matched units, while seed families provide a distribution that must be modeled correctly.

Randomization reduces systematic bias, and blocking groups units that share a known gradient such as bench, room zone, field strip, irrigation line, harvest date, or drying rack. Check cultivars connect trials across time and location. Border plants and guard rows can reduce edge effects. Trial maps must be preserved so spatial trends can be inspected rather than averaged away.

Genotype-by-environment interaction occurs when relative performance changes across environments. A line can be broadly adapted, specifically adapted, or unstable. Multi-environment trials should represent target production systems, not merely the easiest rooms. Management deviations, missing plants, pest events, instrument failures, and selective harvests belong in the dataset. Statistical significance does not replace effect size, uncertainty, biological relevance, or repeatability.
cultivationRelevance: Use a written trial protocol and analysis plan before planting. Define the experimental unit, replication, blocks, randomization, checks, exclusions, and primary outcomes.
measureAndRecord: Before evaluating replicated trials and environmental noise, record the breeding population, generation, identities, and measurement context, including Trial ID/version, genotypes/families, experimental units, randomization seed and map. Keep definitions and identifiers stable so ancestry, family, and phenotype records remain comparable across generations.

During evaluation, track blocks/checks, environments, management, measurements and timing together with the mating design, environment, developmental stage, replicate or family structure, and any selection event that could alter interpretation. Preserve raw values and rejected or missing cases rather than only the selected outcome.

At the decision point, document missing/dead units, deviations, statistical model, effect estimates and intervals.. State the evidence supporting advancement, note uncertainty and correlated tradeoffs, and retain enough pedigree and sample traceability to reconstruct the decision later.
misconceptions: Ten measurements from one plant are ten replicates. This ignores segregation, environmental effects, sampling error, and the possibility that the observed phenotype does not transmit predictably to progeny.

Clones eliminate environmental variation. A label, generation name, or single phenotype does not establish genetic value by itself; use family, progeny, marker, or replicated performance evidence appropriate to the trait.

A significant result from one room proves broad adaptation. The claim should not be generalized beyond the tested population, parents, environments, and measurement methods without additional validation.
evidenceLimits: Inference is limited to sampled genotypes, environments, management, measurement methods, and valid experimental units. Expected genetic ratios, breeding values, and response magnitudes are model- and population-dependent, so they should not be presented as guaranteed outcomes for untested parents or environments.

Evidence from markers, pedigrees, replicated phenotypes, progeny tests, and laboratory assays answers different questions. Strong release claims require the relevant evidence type, adequate sample size, traceable methods, and confirmation that the result persists in the target breeding population and environment.

knowledgeCheck: For "Replicated Trials and Environmental Noise", which records are required to make the result traceable and decision-ready, and which missing field would most weaken the conclusion?

A learner claims, "Ten measurements from one plant are ten replicates." Use the lesson's science and evidence limits to explain why that claim is unreliable, then name one observation or measurement that could separate the competing explanations.

Applied case — Use a written trial protocol and analysis plan before planting. Define the experimental unit, replication, blocks, randomization, checks, exclusions, and primary outcomes. Build a verification plan using the lesson's record set (Trial ID/version; genotypes/families; experimental units; randomization seed and map; blocks/checks; environments; management; measurements and timing; missing/dead units; deviations; statistical model; effect estimates and intervals.). What would you compare before and after the action, and what result would make you revise the original interpretation?
